correctness.rationale: Balanced strongly connected q-ary edge graph; rooted BEST normalizes cyclic rotations. Contracting only forced weight-two arcs preserves rooted arborescences. Its reduced Laplacian splits into q-2 independent color-difference blocks each triangular with q diagonal and a uniform index block. Weighted Matrix-Tree and a complete trapping-interval analysis give determinant q^floor((n-1)/2). The product yields the stated formula for every q>=3,n>=2. Full-graph exact Bareiss determinants and independent exhaustive local-Euler-order checks corroborate parameter cases (see embedded verify.py and verification_output.txt); finite checks are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The nonbinary exact enumeration, unlike the known binary weight-at-most-two formula, is not contained in the inspected primary statements. The 2026 nonbinary paper establishes existence only; the 2012 source concerns binary existence; the full 1993 Fredricksen article explicitly counts the binary t=2 case, so the claim excludes q=2. The 2022/2023 source restricts its investigated sequences to binary alphabets and reports some small experiments. Searched published mathematical records showed no exact q>=3 count. A plausible publisher main text was not accessible, so originality is conditional on the inspected evidence and unresolved indexing risk, rather than asserted independently certified.
residual_risks: A differently indexed prior paper might contain a q-ary exact Euler-tour count in alternative shift-register terminology.
The subscription-protected main body of Li–Jiang–Lin (2022/2023) was not available; its visible statements and abstract are specifically binary, but no claim is made of full-text noncoverage.
No independent literature or scientific audit has yet been performed.

value.rationale: An exact infinite-family count of nonbinary weight-constrained universal cycles is a natural next invariant after recent nonbinary existence theorems. It distinguishes labelled alphabets and rotation normalization, and produces a nontrivial multiplicative closed form depending on both span and alphabet size. Color-decomposed arborescence analysis supplies an independent structural insight; the result is not an arbitrary tiny numerical gain or a binary restatement.
